claim: VivosX is an in vivo disulfide crosslinking approach that utilizes a pair of strategically positioned cysteines on two proteins to probe physical interactions within cells.
source: VivosX is an in vivo disulfide crosslinking approach that utilizes a pair of strategically positioned cysteines on two proteins to probe physical interactions within cells.
evidence: This is a definitional statement from the abstract describing the VivosX method.

claim: Histone H2A.Z often replaces one or both copies of H2A in nucleosomes downstream of promoters.
source: Histone H2A.Z, which often replaces one or both copies of H2A in nucleosomes downstream of promoters, was used to validate VivosX.
evidence: This is established knowledge about H2A.Z localization in chromatin.

claim: Disulfide crosslinks between cysteine-modified H2A.Z and/or H2A histones within nucleosomes were induced using a membrane-permeable oxidant.
source: Disulfide crosslinks between cysteine-modified H2A.Z and/or H2A histones within nucleosomes were induced using a membrane-permeable oxidant.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: VivosX detected different combinations of H2A.Z and H2A within nucleosomes in yeast cells.
source: VivosX detected different combinations of H2A.Z and H2A within nucleosomes in yeast cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VivosX correctly reported the change in global H2A.Z occupancy previously observed when the deposition and eviction pathways of H2A.Z were perturbed.
source: This assay correctly reported the change in global H2A.Z occupancy previously observed when the deposition and eviction pathways of H2A.Z were perturbed.
evidence: This is a validation finding comparing VivosX results to previously published data.

claim: Homotypic H2A.Z/H2A.Z (ZZ) nucleosomes accumulated when assembly of the transcription preinitiation complex was blocked.
source: Homotypic H2A.Z/H2A.Z (ZZ) nucleosomes accumulated when assembly of the transcription preinitiation complex was blocked, revealing that the transcription machinery preferentially disassembles ZZ nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the TBP-FRB depletion experiments.

claim: The transcription machinery preferentially disassembles ZZ nucleosomes.
source: Homotypic H2A.Z/H2A.Z (ZZ) nucleosomes accumulated when assembly of the transcription preinitiation complex was blocked, revealing that the transcription machinery preferentially disassembles ZZ nucleosomes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing ZZ accumulation when PIC assembly is blocked.

claim: VivosX works in human cells.
source: VivosX works in human cells and distinguishes ZZ nucleosomes with one or two ubiquitin moieties, demonstrating that it can be used to detect protein-protein interactions inside cells from different species.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experiments in MCF10A cells shown in Figure 6.

claim: VivosX distinguishes ZZ nucleosomes with one or two ubiquitin moieties.
source: VivosX works in human cells and distinguishes ZZ nucleosomes with one or two ubiquitin moieties, demonstrating that it can be used to detect protein-protein interactions inside cells from different species.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6 where different crosslinked species with ubiquitin modifications are detected.

claim: VivosX can be used to detect protein-protein interactions inside cells from different species.
source: VivosX works in human cells and distinguishes ZZ nucleosomes with one or two ubiquitin moieties, demonstrating that it can be used to detect protein-protein interactions inside cells from different species.
evidence: This is demonstrated by successful application in both yeast and human cells.

claim: Existing cell-based protein-protein interaction assays such as yeast two-hybrid or protein-fragment complementation do not provide information about the site of interaction or the proportion of free versus bound species.
source: Existing cell-based, protein-protein interaction assays, such as yeast two-hybrid or protein-fragment complementation, do not provide information about the site of interaction or the proportion of free versus bound species (Fields and Sternglanz, 1994; Michnick et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a limitation of existing methods cited from the literature.

claim: VivosX uses structural information to guide the placement of a pair of cysteine probes on the opposite sides of a contact site such that they fall within disulfide crosslinking distance when the two proteins interact.
source: VivosX uses structural information to guide the placement of a pair of cysteine probes on the opposite sides of a contact site such that they fall within disulfide crosslinking distance when the two proteins interact.
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of VivosX.

claim: Disulfide adducts do not accumulate naturally due to the reducing environment of the nucleus and cytosol.
source: The disulfide adducts do not accumulate naturally due to the reducing environment of the nucleus and cytosol (Dardalhon et al., 2012; Østergaard et al., 2004), but will do so under oxidizing conditions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cellular redox environment cited from the literature.

claim: Disulfide adducts will accumulate under oxidizing conditions.
source: The disulfide adducts do not accumulate naturally due to the reducing environment of the nucleus and cytosol (Dardalhon et al., 2012; Østergaard et al., 2004), but will do so under oxidizing conditions.
evidence: This is the basis for the VivosX method using 4-DPS treatment.

claim: The canonical nucleosome structure consists of ~150 basepair DNA wrapped around an octameric histone core with two copies of each H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.
source: The canonical view of the nucleosome structure, in which a ~150 basepair DNA wraps around an octameric histone core with two copies of each H2A, H2B, H3, and H4 (Luger et al., 1997), represents only one of the many facets of the basic packaging unit of chromatin in a living cell (Luger et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about nucleosomes cited from the literature.

claim: Nucleosomes in the vicinity of promoters are subjected to a variety of chromatin remodeling activities that alter not only nucleosome conformation, but also histone core composition.
source: Nucleosomes in the vicinity of promoters, for example, are subjected to a variety of chromatin remodeling activities that alter not only nucleosome conformation, but also histone core composition (Clapier et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about chromatin remodeling cited from the literature.

claim: The nucleosome immediately downstream of an RNA polymerase II promoter is often installed with one or two copies of the variant histone H2A.Z in place of H2A.
source: To promote transcription of a gene, the nucleosome immediately downstream of an RNA polymerase II promoter is often installed with one or two copies of the variant histone H2A.Z in place of H2A (Luk et al., 2010; Tramantano et al., 2016; Weber et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about H2A.Z localization cited from the literature.

claim: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-based techniques have been instrumental in uncovering the dynamic interactions of a specific type or post-translationally modified histone with DNA.
source: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-based techniques have been instrumental in uncovering the dynamic interactions of a specific type or post-translationally modified histone with DNA (Gilmour and Lis, 1984; O'Neill and Turner, 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ChIP techniques cited from the literature.

claim: It remains technically challenging to distinguish nucleosomes containing different combinations of histones (e.g. homotypic H2A.Z/H2A.Z versus heterotypic H2A/H2A.Z nucleosomes).
source: It remains technically challenging to distinguish nucleosomes containing different combinations of histones (e.g. homotypic H2A.Z/H2A.Z versus heterotypic H2A/H2A.Z nucleosomes).
evidence: This is a stated limitation of existing methods that motivated the development of VivosX.

claim: Disulfide crosslinking of strategically positioned cysteines on reconstituted nucleosomes or endogenously purified histone substrates in vitro has generated important structural and molecular insights.
source: Disulfide crosslinking of strategically positioned cysteines on reconstituted nucleosomes or endogenously purified histone substrates in vitro has generated important structural and molecular insights.
evidence: This is a summary of prior work using disulfide crosslinking in vitro.

claim: Crosslinking of cysteine probes substituted at the basic N-terminal tail of H4 and the acidic patch of H2A demonstrated the direct interaction between the histone tail and the histone core of neighboring nucleosomes during chromatin fiber compaction.
source: For example, crosslinking of cysteine probes substituted at the basic N-terminal tail of H4 and the acidic patch of H2A demonstrated the direct interaction between the histone tail and the histone core of neighboring nucleosomes during chromatin fiber compaction (Dorigo et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a cited example of prior disulfide crosslinking work.

claim: Disulfide crosslinking between two H3 molecules was used to demonstrate the tetrameric nature of the H3-H4 complex when bound by the histone chaperone Nap1.
source: Disulfide crosslinking between two H3 molecules was used to demonstrate the tetrameric nature of the H3-H4 complex when bound by the histone chaperone Nap1 (Bowman et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a cited example of prior disulfide crosslinking work.

claim: A disulfide crosslinking approach that restricts conformational flexibility of the histone fold domain of H3 and H4 revealed that histone fold distortion is a prerequisite of remodeler-catalyzed histone octamer sliding.
source: A disulfide crosslinking approach that restricts conformational flexibility of the histone fold domain of H3 and H4 revealed that histone fold distortion is a prerequisite of remodeler-catalyzed histone octamer sliding (Sinha et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a cited example of prior disulfide crosslinking work.

claim: Disulfide crosslinking has been applied to stabilize the conformation of nucleosomes to facilitate structural analysis.
source: More recently, disulfide crosslinking has been applied to stabilize the conformation of nucleosomes to facilitate structural analysis (Frouws et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited example of recent disulfide crosslinking work.

claim: The use of disulfide crosslinking to probe protein-protein interactions has been fruitful for the studies of the conformational dynamics of transmembrane proteins, including chemoreceptors and rhodopsin.
source: The use of disulfide crosslinking to probe protein-protein interactions has also been fruitful for the studies of the conformational dynamics of transmembrane proteins, including chemoreceptors and rhodopsin (Falke and Koshland, 1987; Farrens et al., 1996).
evidence: This is a cited example of disulfide crosslinking applications in other protein systems.

claim: Disulfide crosslinking has not been well developed as a general strategy for capturing protein-protein interactions in cells.
source: While disulfide crosslinking has been used successfully in vitro, this approach has not been well developed as a general strategy for capturing protein-protein interactions in cells.
evidence: This is a stated gap in the field that VivosX addresses.

claim: One technical challenge is that the reducing environment inside the cytoplasm and nucleus inhibits disulfide accumulation even when cysteine pairs are within crosslinking distance.
source: One technical challenge is that the reducing environment inside the cytoplasm and nucleus inhibits disulfide accumulation even when cysteine pairs are within crosslinking distance (Dardalhon et al., 2012; Østergaard et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a cited technical challenge for in vivo disulfide crosslinking.

claim: Cysteine pairs can be activated to form disulfide linkages in the presence of a thiol-reactive oxidant, but such reactions are dependent on the accessibility of the thiol groups.
source: Although cysteine pairs can be activated to form disulfide linkages in the presence of a thiol-reactive oxidant, such reactions are dependent on the accessibility of the thiol groups (Johnson et al., 1987).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about the requirements for disulfide formation.

claim: The choice of cysteine probe substitutions must be guided not only by structural information but also conformational dynamics.
source: Thus, the choice of cysteine probe substitutions must be guided not only by structural information but also conformational dynamics.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cited knowledge about thiol accessibility.

claim: H2A.Z is inserted into +1 nucleosomes at promoters of yeast and human cells.
source: At promoters of yeast and human cells, H2A.Z is inserted into +1 nucleosomes, which are located immediately downstream of the transcription start site (Albert et al., 2007; Barski et al., 2007) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from the literature and illustrated in a figure.

claim: In human cells, H2A.Z is also associated with heterochromatin.
source: In human cells, H2A.Z is also associated with heterochromatin (Rangasamy et al., 2003).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about H2A.Z localization in human cells.

claim: Heterochromatic H2A.Z is generally monoubiquitylated at the C-terminus.
source: Unlike H2A.Z found in euchromatin, heterochromatic H2A.Z is generally monoubiquitylated at the C-terminus (Sarcinella et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about H2A.Z modification in heterochromatin.

claim: SWR catalyzes H2A.Z deposition via a histone exchange mechanism driven by ATP hydrolysis.
source: SWR, a multi-subunit chromatin remodeler, catalyzes H2A.Z deposition via a histone exchange mechanism driven by ATP hydrolysis (Mizuguchi et al., 2004).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about the SWR complex mechanism.

claim: SWR removes an H2A-H2B dimer and concomitantly inserts H2A.Z-H2B onto each face of the nucleosome, thereby converting the canonical H2A/H2A (AA) nucleosome to the heterotypic H2A/H2A.Z (AZ) nucleosomal intermediate before forming the homotypic H2A.Z/H2A.Z (ZZ) nucleosomal product.
source: SWR removes an H2A-H2B dimer and concomitantly inserts H2A.Z-H2B onto each face of the nucleosome, thereby converting the canonical H2A/H2A (AA) nucleosome to the heterotypic H2A/H2A.Z (AZ) nucleosomal intermediate before forming the homotypic H2A.Z/H2A.Z (ZZ) nucleosomal product (Luk et al., 2010) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about the SWR mechanism illustrated in a figure.

claim: H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes are preferentially disassembled via a process that is dependent on the preinitiation complex (PIC).
source: H2A.Z-containing nucleosomes are preferentially disassembled via a process that is dependent on the preinitiation complex (PIC), although it is unclear whether the ZZ or the AZ species are equally targeted for disassembly (Tramantano et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about H2A.Z eviction.

claim: Within an AA, AZ or ZZ nucleosome, the two L1 loop regions of the histone fold domains of the opposing H2A and/or H2A.Z molecules come into contact with each other at an interface that passes through the nucleosomal dyad.
source: Within an AA, AZ or ZZ nucleosome, the two L1 loop regions of the histone fold domains of the opposing H2A and/or H2A.Z molecules come into contact with each other at an interface that passes through the nucleosomal dyad, but not when the histones are outside of the nucleosomal structure (Luger et al., 1997; Suto et al., 2000) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is structural knowledge cited from the literature and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The L1 loop regions of H2A and/or H2A.Z do not come into contact when the histones are outside of the nucleosomal structure.
source: Within an AA, AZ or ZZ nucleosome, the two L1 loop regions of the histone fold domains of the opposing H2A and/or H2A.Z molecules come into contact with each other at an interface that passes through the nucleosomal dyad, but not when the histones are outside of the nucleosomal structure (Luger et al., 1997; Suto et al., 2000) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is structural knowledge cited from the literature and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The L1-L1' interface is ideal for the placement of cysteine probes for in vivo disulfide crosslinking.
source: Thus, the L1-L1' (prime represents the symmetrical nucleosomal counterpart) interface is ideal for the placement of cysteine probes for in vivo disulfide crosslinking.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural knowledge about the L1-L1' interface.

claim: Only when histones are inserted into nucleosomes will the cysteine pairs be close enough to form disulfide bonds.
source: The assumption is that only when histones are inserted into nucleosomes will the cysteine pairs be close enough to form disulfide bonds, allowing crosslinking efficiency to act as a metric for the global occupancy of H2A and H2A.Z (these histones naturally lack cysteine).
evidence: This is a stated assumption underlying the VivosX approach.

claim: H2A and H2A.Z naturally lack cysteine.
source: The assumption is that only when histones are inserted into nucleosomes will the cysteine pairs be close enough to form disulfide bonds, allowing crosslinking efficiency to act as a metric for the global occupancy of H2A and H2A.Z (these histones naturally lack cysteine).
evidence: This is stated knowledge about the amino acid composition of H2A and H2A.Z.

claim: All six HTZ1(Cys)FL alleles fully complemented the formamide sensitivity of the htz1∆ mutant.
source: All six HTZ1(Cys)FL alleles fully complemented the formamide sensitivity of the htz1∆ mutant (Figure 1C) (Wu et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a functional complementation result shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Wild-type core histones of yeast do not contain any cysteine.
source: Since wild-type core histones of yeast do not contain any cysteine, the Htz1(Cys)FL protein contributes the only sulfhydryl group to the nucleosome.
evidence: This is stated knowledge about yeast histone composition.

claim: The Htz1(Cys)FL protein contributes the only sulfhydryl group to the nucleosome.
source: Since wild-type core histones of yeast do not contain any cysteine, the Htz1(Cys)FL protein contributes the only sulfhydryl group to the nucleosome.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the fact that wild-type yeast histones lack cysteine.

claim: In the presence of 4-DPS, the H2A.Z-to-H2A.Z crosslinking adducts (ZxZ), which migrate at ~37 kD, were detected for cysteines substituted at A45, T46, G47 and R48, but not H44 or T49.
source: In the presence of 4-DPS, the H2A.Z-to-H2A.Z crosslinking adducts (ZxZ), which migrate at ~37 kD, were detected for cysteines substituted at A45, T46, G47 and R48, but not H44 or T49 (Figure 1D–E, top panels).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: The disulfide crosslinking efficiency does not correlate particularly well with Cα-Cα' proximity.
source: The disulfide crosslinking efficiency, which is defined as the ratio of ZxZ over total H2A.Z immunoblotting signals, does not correlate particularly well with Cα-Cα' proximity, suggesting that the L1-L1' interface is dynamic (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The L1-L1' interface is dynamic.
source: The disulfide crosslinking efficiency, which is defined as the ratio of ZxZ over total H2A.Z immunoblotting signals, does not correlate particularly well with Cα-Cα' proximity, suggesting that the L1-L1' interface is dynamic (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lack of correlation between crosslinking efficiency and Cα-Cα' distance.

claim: The formation of the ZxZ adduct for A45C, T46C, G47C, and R48C was accompanied by a reduction in the FLAG-tagged Htz1(Cys)FL monomer (mono Z) at ~17 kD.
source: The formation of the ZxZ adduct for A45C, T46C, G47C, and R48C was accompanied by a reduction in the FLAG-tagged Htz1(Cys)FL monomer (mono Z) at ~17 kD (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: Under reducing SDS-PAGE conditions where β-mercaptoethanol (β-ME) was added to the gel loading buffer, all ZxZ adducts were cleaved and the Htz1(Cys)FL mutant proteins migrated as monomers.
source: Under reducing SDS-PAGE conditions where β-mercaptoethanol (β-ME) was added to the gel loading buffer, all ZxZ adducts were cleaved and the Htz1(Cys)FL mutant proteins migrated as monomers (Figure 1D–E, bottom panels).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E demonstrating that the adducts are disulfide-bonded.

claim: The HTZ1(T46C)FL mutant was chosen for subsequent VivosX experiments because it also efficiently crosslinked to an L1' cysteine mutant in H2A.
source: The HTZ1(T46C)FL mutant was chosen for subsequent VivosX experiments because it also efficiently crosslinked to an L1' cysteine mutant in H2A (see below).
evidence: This is a stated rationale for the choice of mutant for further experiments.

claim: The effectiveness of the NEM blocking step was confirmed by the inhibition of total protein labeling with the thiol-specific fluorescence reagent, Alexa647-maleimide.
source: The effectiveness of the NEM blocking step was confirmed by the inhibition of total protein labeling with the thiol-specific fluorescence reagent, Alexa647-maleimide (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, compare Lanes 1 and 3) and by the inhibition of formation of non-specific disulfide crosslinking adducts of Htz1(T46C)FL (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, compare Lanes 1 and 3).
evidence: This is experimental validation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The effectiveness of the NEM blocking step was confirmed by the inhibition of formation of non-specific disulfide crosslinking adducts of Htz1(T46C)FL.
source: The effectiveness of the NEM blocking step was confirmed by the inhibition of total protein labeling with the thiol-specific fluorescence reagent, Alexa647-maleimide (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A, compare Lanes 1 and 3) and by the inhibition of formation of non-specific disulfide crosslinking adducts of Htz1(T46C)FL (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, compare Lanes 1 and 3).
evidence: This is experimental validation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The duration for the extraction of precipitated histones by the TUNES buffer was empirically determined to be 60 min as it allows maximal solubilization of the histones without any appreciable reduction of the disulfide adducts.
source: The duration for the extraction of precipitated histones by the TUNES buffer was empirically determined to be 60 min as it allows maximal solubilization of the histones without any appreciable reduction of the disulfide adducts (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C–D).
evidence: This is an optimization result shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C-D.

claim: All immunoblots were conducted using a pan-H2A antibody (Active Motif) since this antibody gave a stronger signal than the V5 antibody.
source: Although the mutated HTA1(Cys) alleles contain an N-terminal fusion to the V5 epitope, all immunoblots below were conducted using a pan-H2A antibody (Active Motif) since this antibody gave a stronger signal than the V5 antibody (not shown).
evidence: This is a stated methodological choice based on antibody performance.

claim: All five V5HTA1(Cys) mutants rescued the inviability caused by loss of the URA3 plasmid, indicating that H2A function was not impaired by the cysteine substitutions.
source: This inviability was rescued by each one of the V5HTA1(Cys) mutants carried on the HIS3 plasmid, indicating that H2A function was not impaired by the cysteine substitutions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is functional complementation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: AxA crosslink adducts were observed for the H2A N39C, Y40C, A41C, and Q42C mutant proteins, but not G38C.
source: Using the VivosX method described above but probing with anti-H2A antibodies, AxA crosslink adducts were observed for the H2A N39C, Y40C, A41C, and Q42C mutant proteins, but not G38C (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: The lack of G38C crosslinking can be explained by a long Cα-Cα' distance (13.2 Å).
source: While the lack of G38C crosslinking can be explained by a long Cα-Cα' distance (13.2 Å), the crosslinking efficiency of the other four H2A L1 loop sites does not correlate well with Cα-Cα' proximity (Figure 2E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) (White et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data based on structural information cited from White et al., 2001.

claim: The crosslinking efficiency of the other four H2A L1 loop sites does not correlate well with Cα-Cα' proximity.
source: While the lack of G38C crosslinking can be explained by a long Cα-Cα' distance (13.2 Å), the crosslinking efficiency of the other four H2A L1 loop sites does not correlate well with Cα-Cα' proximity (Figure 2E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) (White et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: A41C and Q42C exhibited robust crosslinking despite having a Cα-Cα' distance of >10 Å.
source: In fact, A41C and Q42C exhibited robust crosslinking despite having a Cα-Cα' distance of >10 Å.
evidence: This is an observation from the data highlighting the lack of correlation between distance and crosslinking efficiency.

claim: An increase in AxA adducts was accompanied by a reciprocal decrease in monomeric H2A (mono A) in a 4-DPS-dependent manner.
source: Similar to Htz1(Cys)FL, an increase in AxA adducts was accompanied by a reciprocal decrease in monomeric H2A (mono A) in a 4-DPS-dependent manner (Figure 2C–D, top panels and Figure 2E).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D and Figure 2E.

claim: The AxA species was lost when the proteins were exposed to β-ME, further confirming that AxA is caused by disulfide crosslinking at the cysteine sites.
source: The AxA species was lost when the proteins were exposed to β-ME, further confirming that AxA is caused by disulfide crosslinking at the cysteine sites (Figure 2C–D, bottom panel).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 2C-D demonstrating that the adducts are disulfide-bonded.

claim: Low levels of AxA crosslinks were detected for N39C, Y40C, A41C and Q42C even in the absence of 4-DPS.
source: Note that low levels of AxA crosslinks were detected for N39C, Y40C, A41C and Q42C even in the absence of 4-DPS. This may reflect the natural redox state of the nucleus (Dardalhon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an observation from the data with a speculative interpretation.

claim: Low levels of AxA crosslinks in the absence of 4-DPS may reflect the natural redox state of the nucleus.
source: Note that low levels of AxA crosslinks were detected for N39C, Y40C, A41C and Q42C even in the absence of 4-DPS. This may reflect the natural redox state of the nucleus (Dardalhon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the background crosslinking observed.

claim: For the V5HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C)FL double mutant, two crosslinked species were observed when the blots were probed with either anti-FLAG or anti-H2A to detect H2A.Z and H2A, respectively.
source: For the V5HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C)FL double mutant, two crosslinked species were observed when the blots were probed with either anti-FLAG or anti-H2A to detect H2A.Z and H2A, respectively (Figure 3A, lane 6 and Figure 3B, lane 6).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: For H2A.Z, the top band exhibited the same mobility as ZxZ.
source: In each case, one band of the doublet co-migrated with the homotypic adduct. For H2A.Z, the top band exhibited the same mobility as ZxZ (Figure 3A, lanes 6 and 8), while the lower band of the H2A doublet co-migrated with AxA.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The lower band of the H2A doublet co-migrated with AxA.
source: In each case, one band of the doublet co-migrated with the homotypic adduct. For H2A.Z, the top band exhibited the same mobility as ZxZ (Figure 3A, lanes 6 and 8), while the lower band of the H2A doublet co-migrated with AxA.
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The differences in ZxZ and AxA mobility are consistent with the observation that monomeric Htz1(T46C)FL migrates slower than monomeric V5Hta1(N39C) despite the fact that the calculated molecular weight of Htz1(T46C)FL is actually smaller (16.6 kD versus 16.8 kD), possibly due to the strong negative charge of the FLAG epitope.
source: The differences in ZxZ and AxA mobility are consistent with the observation that monomeric Htz1(T46C)FL migrates slower than monomeric V5Hta1(N39C) despite the fact that the calculated molecular weight of Htz1(T46C)FL is actually smaller (16.6 kD versus 16.8 kD), possibly due to the strong negative charge of the FLAG epitope (Figure 3A–B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is an observation from the data with a speculative explanation.

claim: A doublet was observed only when V5HTA1(N39C) and HTZ1(T46C)FL were combined, suggesting that one band of the doublet represents V5Hta1(N39C) crosslinked to Htz1(T46C)FL (AxZ).
source: A doublet was observed only when V5HTA1(N39C) and HTZ1(T46C)FL were combined, suggesting that one band of the doublet represents V5Hta1(N39C) crosslinked to Htz1(T46C)FL (AxZ) (Figure 3A–B, lane 6).
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: Realignment of the two halves of the blot demonstrated that the predicted AxZ band contains both V5Hta1 and Htz1FL and runs between the ZxZ and AxA adducts.
source: Realignment of the two halves of the blot demonstrated that the predicted AxZ band contains both V5Hta1 and Htz1FL and runs between the ZxZ and AxA adducts (Figure 3C, top panel).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3C confirming the identity of the AxZ band.

claim: All the crosslinked proteins were eliminated when fractionated on a gel in the presence of β-ME, confirming that, similar to ZxZ and AxA, the AxZ adduct was also generated by disulfide crosslinking.
source: All the crosslinked proteins were eliminated when fractionated on a gel in the presence of β-ME, confirming that, similar to ZxZ and AxA, the AxZ adduct was also generated by disulfide crosslinking (Figure 3C, bottom panel).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3C demonstrating that the AxZ adduct is disulfide-bonded.

claim: The assumption is that only histones in close proximity in assembled nucleosomes will crosslink and therefore the AxA, AxZ, and ZxZ signals derived from whole cell extracts accurately reflect the native AA, AZ and ZZ nucleosomal levels.
source: An advantage of VivosX is that it uses whole cell extracts, thereby obviating the need to purify chromatin, which greatly facilitates high-throughput experiments. The assumption is that only histones in close proximity in assembled nucleosomes will crosslink and therefore the AxA, AxZ, and ZxZ signals derived from whole cell extracts accurately reflect the native AA, AZ and ZZ nucleosomal levels.
evidence: This is a stated assumption underlying the VivosX approach.

claim: Similar ratios of the various crosslinked species should be observed when native nucleosomes are extracted from cells before they are used for crosslinking.
source: If true, then similar ratios of the various crosslinked species should be observed when native nucleosomes are extracted from cells before they are used for crosslinking.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the assumption that whole cell extracts accurately reflect nucleosomal levels.

claim: The ratios of AxZ to ZxZ (1:0.2) or AxZ to AxA (1:3.5) in native nucleosomes were similar to those observed with the V5HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C)FL double mutant using total extracts (1:0.3 and 1:4.2, respectively).
source: The ratios of AxZ to ZxZ (1:0.2) or AxZ to AxA (1:3.5) in native nucleosomes (Figure 3D, lanes 3 and 5) were similar to those observed with the V5HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C)FL double mutant using total extracts (1:0.3 and 1:4.2, respectively) (Figure 3A–C, averaged values).
evidence: This is a comparison of data from Figure 3D with Figure 3A-C validating the whole cell extract approach.

claim: Higher levels of the AxA, AxZ, and ZxZ adducts were present in native nucleosomes than whole cell extracts of the untreated cells.
source: Higher levels of the AxA, AxZ, and ZxZ adducts were present in native nucleosomes than whole cell extracts of the untreated cells (Figure 3D, 4-DPS minus lanes).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The higher background oxidation in native nucleosomes was likely due to atmospheric oxidation of the dithiols during the cell lysis, chromatin preparation and/or MNase digestion steps.
source: This difference was likely due to atmospheric oxidation of the dithiols during the cell lysis, chromatin preparation and/or MNase digestion steps.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the higher background in native nucleosomes.

claim: Such background oxidation was minimized in the whole cell extracts as cells were fixed by TCA and extraction was performed in the presence of the thiol blocker NEM.
source: Such background oxidation was minimized in the whole cell extracts as cells were fixed by TCA and extraction was performed in the presence of the thiol blocker NEM.
evidence: This is an explanation for why whole cell extracts have lower background oxidation.

claim: In the absence of SWC5, H2A.Z levels at promoters are decreased.
source: SWC5 encodes a component of the SWR complex that is required for its H2A.Z deposition activity at promoters (Tramantano et al., 2016). In the absence of SWC5, H2A.Z levels at promoters are decreased (Tramantano et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about the effect of SWC5 deletion.

claim: ZxZ adducts were observed in the extracts from the SWC5 strain, but not swc5∆.
source: ZxZ adducts were observed in the extracts from the SWC5 strain, but not swc5∆ (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Mutants swc5(1-232) and swc5(LDW→3A) significantly reduced ZxZ crosslinking efficiency in VivosX.
source: Additional mutants of SWC5 that were previously shown to prevent H2A.Z deposition include a truncation of the highly conserved BCNT domain [swc5(1-232)] and substitution of the LDW motif within BCNT with alanines [swc5(LDW→3A)] (Sun and Luk, 2017) (Figure 4A). These mutants also significantly reduced ZxZ crosslinking efficiency in VivosX (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 4B-C.

claim: swc5∆ HTZ1(T46C)FL carrying SWC5 on a plasmid has a lower ZxZ crosslinking efficiency than HTZ1(T46C)FL with endogenous SWC5.
source: Note that swc5∆ HTZ1(T46C)FL carrying SWC5 on a plasmid has a lower ZxZ crosslinking efficiency than HTZ1(T46C)FL with endogenous SWC5 (compare Figure 4 to Figure 1F).
evidence: This is an observation comparing data from Figure 4 to Figure 1F.

claim: The discrepancy in ZxZ crosslinking efficiency could be due to loss of the SWC5 plasmid in a fraction of cells during growth of the culture.
source: The discrepancy could be due to loss of the SWC5 plasmid in a fraction of cells during growth of the culture.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed difference.

claim: ZZ nucleosomes are normally removed from the +1 position at promoters by formation of the transcriptional preinitiation complex (PIC).
source: ZZ nucleosomes are normally removed from the +1 position at promoters by formation of the transcriptional preinitiation complex (PIC) (Tramantano et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about ZZ nucleosome eviction.

claim: ZZ nucleosomes accumulate when their disassembly is inhibited by depletion of the TATA-binding protein (TBP), which is required for PIC recruitment.
source: As a result, ZZ nucleosomes accumulate when their disassembly is inhibited by depletion of the TATA-binding protein (TBP), which is required for PIC recruitment (Hahn, 2004).
evidence: This is a logical inference from the cited knowledge about TBP's role in PIC recruitment.

claim: A reproducible increase of ZxZ adducts and a concomitant decrease of mono Z was observed after TBP-FRB depletion.
source: A reproducible increase of ZxZ adducts and a concomitant decrease of mono Z was observed after TBP-FRB depletion (N = 3), consistent with our earlier quantitative ChIP-seq results (Figure 5A, compare lanes 6 and 8) (Tramantano et al., 2016).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5A consistent with prior ChIP-seq results.

claim: ZxZ crosslinks were reduced when SWC5-FRB was depleted by Anchor-away.
source: By contrast, ZxZ crosslinks were reduced when SWC5-FRB was depleted by Anchor-away (N = 3) (Figure 5A, lanes 10 and 12).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: VivosX can accurately report the global chromatin dynamics of H2A.Z.
source: VivosX can therefore accurately report the global chromatin dynamics of H2A.Z.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing VivosX correctly reports changes in H2A.Z occupancy.

claim: Blocking PIC assembly by depleting TBP-FRB preferentially increased the ZxZ adduct, indicating that ZZ nucleosomes, but not AZ nucleosomes, were targeted by PIC for removal.
source: Blocking PIC assembly by depleting TBP-FRB preferentially increased the ZxZ adduct, indicating that ZZ nucleosomes, but not AZ nucleosomes, were targeted by PIC for removal (Figure 5B–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claim: Monomeric H2A.Z is diminished reciprocally when ZZ nucleosomes accumulate, consistent with the free pool of Z-B dimers being used by SWR to generate more ZZ nucleosomes, but without being replenished by PIC-dependent ZZ nucleosome disassembly.
source: In fact, monomeric H2A.Z is diminished reciprocally, consistent with the free pool of Z-B dimers being used by SWR to generate more ZZ nucleosomes, but without being replenished by PIC-dependent ZZ nucleosome disassembly (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data with reference to the model in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The increase in the ZxZ adduct and the corresponding decrease in monomeric H2A.Z were small but reproducible in three biological replicates and statistically significant, with non-overlapping standard deviations and p values of < 0.05 based on t-tests.
source: While the increase in the ZxZ adduct and the corresponding decrease in monomeric H2A.Z were small, these differences were reproducible in three biological replicates and statistically significant, with non-overlapping standard deviations and p values of < 0.05 based on t-tests.
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the data demonstrating significance.

claim: Human H2A.Z has two isoforms (H2A.Z.1 and H2A.Z.2), and they are encoded by the H2AFZ and H2AFV genes, respectively.
source: Human H2A.Z has two isoforms (H2A.Z.1 and H2A.Z.2), and they are encoded by the H2AFZ and H2AFV genes, respectively (Vardabasso et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about human H2A.Z isoforms.

claim: H2A.Z(H43C) corresponds to the yeast Htz1(R48C), which has a similar crosslinking efficiency as the Htz1(T46C) used in most yeast experiments.
source: H2A.Z(H43C) corresponds to the yeast Htz1(R48C), which has a similar crosslinking efficiency as the Htz1(T46C) used in most yeast experiments (Figure 1B and F).
evidence: This is a comparison based on data shown in Figure 1B and F.

claim: H2A.Z(H43C) was chosen for human VivosX, instead of H2A.Z(T41C), because the crosslinking efficiency of Htz1(R48C) was slightly better than Htz1(T46C) in preliminary experiments.
source: H2A.Z(H43C) was chosen for human VivosX, instead of H2A.Z(T41C) [cognate amino acid of yeast (T46C)] because the crosslinking efficiency of Htz1(R48C) was slightly better than Htz1(T46C) in our preliminary experiments (data not shown).
evidence: This is a stated rationale for the choice of mutant for human experiments.

claim: The H2A.Z(H43C)V5 protein exhibited a more complex pattern of crosslinked proteins than yeast Htz1(T46C)FL.
source: The H2A.Z(H43C)V5 protein exhibited a more complex pattern of crosslinked proteins than yeast Htz1(T46C)FL (Figure 6A, lane 4).
evidence: This is an observation from the data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Four slower migrating bands appeared above the expected monomeric H2A.Z(H43C)V5.
source: Four slower migrating bands appeared above the expected monomeric H2A.Z(H43C)V5.
evidence: This is an observation from the data in Figure 6A.

claim: The top three bands in H2A.Z(H43C)V5 lane were disulfide adducts that occur at the H43C position because these bands were not observed in the cells expressing wild-type H2A.ZV5.
source: The top three bands in H2A.Z(H43C)V5 lane were disulfide adducts that occur at the H43C position because these bands were not observed in the cells expressing wild-type H2A.ZV5 (Figure 6A, compare lanes 2 and 4).
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: When the same lysate of H2A.Z(H43C)V5 was treated with β-ME, the top three bands disappeared.
source: In addition, when the same lysate of H2A.Z(H43C)V5 was treated with β-ME, these three bands disappeared (compare Lane four in Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 6A-B demonstrating that the bands are disulfide-bonded.

claim: The H2A.Z band near the 25 kD marker could represent a ubiquitylated form of H2A.Z.
source: Since the H2A.Z band near the 25 kD marker is not due to crosslinking, it could represent a ubiquitylated form of H2A.Z, as suggested by Sarcinella et al. (2007).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on cited literature.

claim: Mutation of two ubiquitylation sites at K120 and K121 to arginines in the H2AFZV5 and H2AFZ(H43C)V5 alleles reduced the amount of the ~25 kD band in the absence of 4-DPS, indicating that this band represents monoubiquitylated H2A.Z.
source: To test this idea, two (of three) ubiquitylation sites at K120 and K121 were mutated to arginines in the H2AFZV5 and H2AFZ(H43C)V5 alleles. Both mutants reduced the amount of the ~25 kD band in the absence of 4-DPS, indicating that this band represents monoubiquitylated H2A.Z (Figure 6A, lanes 5–8).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 6A confirming the identity of the ubiquitylated band.

claim: The two slowest crosslinked adducts were almost eliminated in the H2AFZ(H43C,KK→RR)V5 mutant, with a corresponding increase in the remaining adduct, suggesting that the ~30 kD band is the ZxZ disulfide adduct of two non-ubiquitylated H2A.Z monomers.
source: The two slowest crosslinked adducts were almost eliminated in the H2AFZ(H43C,KK→RR)V5 mutant, with a corresponding increase in the remaining adduct, suggesting that the ~30 kD band is the ZxZ disulfide adduct of two non-ubiquitylated H2A.Z monomers (Figure 6A, compare lanes 4, 6, and 8).
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The top two bands of the crosslinked H2A.Z(H43C)V5 species are likely ZxZ adducts that are conjugated to one (uZxZ) or two ubiquitin moieties (uZxuZ).
source: Finally, the top two bands of the crosslinked H2A.Z(H43C)V5 species are likely ZxZ adducts that are conjugated to one (uZxZ) or two ubiquitin moieties (uZxuZ).
evidence: This is an inference from the data about the identity of the upper bands.

claim: In H2A.Z(H43C, KK→RR)V5, both of the upper bands were strongly diminished, indicating that these positions are associated with the ubiquitylated forms of H2A.Z.
source: In H2A.Z(H43C, KK→RR)V5, both of these upper bands were strongly diminished, indicating that these positions are associated with the ubiquitylated forms of H2A.Z (Figure 6A, compare lanes 4 and 6).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 6A supporting the identification of ubiquitylated species.

claim: VivosX data suggest that up to two ubiquitin moieties can be simultaneously attached to one ZZ nucleosome.
source: Our VivosX data suggest that up to two ubiquitin moieties can be simultaneously attached to one ZZ nucleosome.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing different ubiquitylated crosslinked species.

claim: The two ubiquitin moieties are separately attached to the opposite faces of the ZZ nucleosome given that reduction of the disulfide bond gave rise to mono- but not di-ubiquitylated H2A.Z.
source: We deduce that the two ubiquitin moieties are separately attached to the opposite faces of the ZZ nucleosome given that reduction of the disulfide bond gave rise to mono- but not di-ubiquitylated H2A.Z.
evidence: This is a deduction from the data showing that reducing conditions produce only monoubiquitylated H2A.Z.

claim: This observation is in concordance with a previous result that showed only one of the three lysines in the 120-KKGQQK-125 motif at the C-terminus of H2A.Z was exclusively ubiquitylated.
source: This observation is in concordance with a previous result that showed only one of the three lysines in the 120-KKGQQK-125 motif at the C-terminus of H2A.Z was exclusively ubiquitylated (Sarcinella et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a comparison with cited literature supporting the interpretation.

claim: Cells with ectopic H2AFZ vector expressed ~5 times more protein than endogenous H2A.Z.
source: In addition, cells with a similar ectopic H2AFZ vector (with an identical promoter but without the V5 tag and cysteine mutation) expressed ~5 times more protein than endogenous H2A.Z (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The higher level of H2A.Z could cause misincorporation and thus the observed unmodified and ubiquitylated H2A.Z levels do not necessarily reflect the in vivo distribution of H2A.Z in the euchromatic and heterochromatic regions.
source: The higher level of H2A.Z could cause misincorporation and thus the observed unmodified and ubiquitylated H2A.Z levels do not necessarily reflect the in vivo distribution of H2A.Z in the euchromatic and heterochromatic regions.
evidence: This is a caveat about the interpretation of the data due to overexpression.

claim: One potential caveat of VivosX is the 'observer effect', where the crosslinking of two histones could potentially perturb in vivo chromatin dynamics.
source: One potential caveat of VivosX is the 'observer effect', where the crosslinking of two histones could potentially perturb in vivo chromatin dynamics.
evidence: This is a stated limitation of the VivosX method.

claim: Z-to-Z crosslinking might interfere with ZZ nucleosome disassembly and thus VivosX may overestimate the in vivo level of ZZ nucleosomes.
source: For example, Z-to-Z crosslinking might interfere with ZZ nucleosome disassembly. As such, VivosX may overestimate the in vivo level of ZZ nucleosomes.
evidence: This is a speculative concern about potential artifacts of the method.

claim: Z-to-A and A-to-A crosslinking could interfere with the H2A.Z deposition function of SWR as the remodeler replaces each of the two nucleosomal A-B dimers with Z-B dimers one at a time.
source: Alternatively but not exclusively, Z-to-A and A-to-A crosslinking could interfere with the H2A.Z deposition function of SWR as the remodeler replaces each of the two nucleosomal A-B dimers with Z-B dimers one at a time (Luk et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a speculative concern about potential artifacts of the method with cited mechanism.

claim: In the experiment where VivosX was used to predict changes in H2A.Z occupancy, H2A.Z eviction or deposition was blocked for at least 1 hr (a duration exceeding the turnover half-life of H2A.Z at a typical promoter) before the induction of crosslinking.
source: Therefore, in the experiment where VivosX was used to predict changes in H2A.Z occupancy (Figure 5), H2A.Z eviction or deposition was blocked for at least 1 hr (a duration exceeding the turnover half-life of H2A.Z at a typical promoter) before the induction of crosslinking (Tramantano et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a stated experimental design consideration to address the observer effect caveat.

claim: Despite precautions, we cannot rule out that the L1-L1' disulfide crosslinking is indirectly interfering with H2A.Z deposition and eviction.
source: Despite this precaution and the fact that H2A.Z VivosX correctly reported the change in H2A.Z occupancy, we cannot rule out that the L1-L1' disulfide crosslinking is indirectly interfering with H2A.Z deposition and eviction.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation despite validation of the method.

claim: 4-DPS could elicit an oxidative stress response as has been observed for other oxidizing agents.
source: A second potential caveat was that 4-DPS, the oxidizing agent used in VivosX, could elicit an oxidative stress response as has been observed for other oxidizing agents (Gasch et al., 2000; Weiner et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a stated concern based on cited literature about oxidative stress responses.

claim: Similar levels of the ZxZ adducts were observed in the presence or absence of azide after 4-DPS treatment, suggesting that bulk Z-to-Z crosslinking is not dramatically affected by the oxidative stress response.
source: In a control experiment, sodium azide was added in conjunction with 4-DPS during the crosslinking step to inhibit ATP-dependent processes, such as transcription and replication. Similar levels of the ZxZ adducts were observed in the presence or absence of azide after 4-DPS treatment, suggesting that bulk Z-to-Z crosslinking is not dramatically affected by the oxidative stress response (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–E), although rearrangement of the genomic ZZ nucleosome occupancy cannot be ruled out.
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D-E addressing the oxidative stress concern.

claim: Rearrangement of the genomic ZZ nucleosome occupancy due to oxidative stress cannot be ruled out.
source: Similar levels of the ZxZ adducts were observed in the presence or absence of azide after 4-DPS treatment, suggesting that bulk Z-to-Z crosslinking is not dramatically affected by the oxidative stress response (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–E), although rearrangement of the genomic ZZ nucleosome occupancy cannot be ruled out.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation despite the control experiment.

claim: The average distance between the two alpha carbon atoms (Cα-Cα') of a disulfide bond is 5.6 Å with a range of 4.3 Å – 6.5 Å.
source: The average distance between the two alpha carbon atoms (Cα-Cα') of a disulfide bond is 5.6 Å with a range of 4.3 Å – 6.5 Å (Schmidt et al., 2006).
evidence: This is cited structural knowledge about disulfide bonds.

claim: It was surprising that multiple positions along the L1 region of H2A and H2A.Z supported robust intra-nucleosomal crosslinking given that some of these positions have Cα-Cα' distances > 7 Å in crystal structures.
source: It was therefore surprising that multiple positions along the L1 region of H2A and H2A.Z supported robust intra-nucleosomal crosslinking given that some of these positions have Cα-Cα' distances > 7 Å in crystal structures (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) (Suto et al., 2000; White et al., 2001).
evidence: This is an observation from the data compared to cited structural information.

claim: Some of the crosslinkable L1 side chains (e.g. Y40 and A41 of H2A) are largely inaccessible to solvent.
source: Furthermore, some of the crosslinkable L1 side chains (e.g. Y40 and A41 of H2A) are largely inaccessible to solvent (Suto et al., 2000; White et al., 2001).
evidence: This is cited structural knowledge about solvent accessibility.

claim: The L1 loop must adopt an alternative conformation from that observed in the crystal structure to allow the inaccessible cysteine thiolate to attack the disulfide of 4-DPS.
source: Given that the thiol-disulfide interchange between cysteine thiols and 4-DPS involves the SN2 nucleophilic substitution mechanism (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A), the L1 loop must adopt an alternative conformation from that observed in the crystal structure to allow the inaccessible cysteine thiolate to attack the disulfide of 4-DPS.
evidence: This is an inference from the chemical mechanism and the observation of crosslinking at inaccessible positions.

claim: The nucleosomal L1-L1' interface between the two H2A.Z and/or H2A is dynamic.
source: We speculate that the nucleosomal L1-L1' interface between the two H2A.Z and/or H2A is dynamic.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the crosslinking data.

claim: The two halves of the nucleosome could transiently open like a clam, as they split between the two DNA gyres while the dyadic DNA region acts as a hinge.
source: It has been proposed that the two halves of the nucleosome could transiently open like a clam, as they split between the two DNA gyres while the dyadic DNA region acts as a hinge (Andrews and Luger, 2011) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about nucleosome dynamics.

claim: Such a clamshell opening motion could further increase the degree of freedom of the L1-L1' interface, promoting VivosX adducts of H2A and H2A.Z.
source: Such a clamshell opening motion could further increase the degree of freedom of the L1-L1' interface, promoting VivosX adducts of H2A and H2A.Z.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed crosslinking efficiency.

claim: The biochemical environment surrounding the cysteine residues can influence disulfide crosslinking efficiency.
source: In addition to the aforementioned solvent accessibility issue, the biochemical environment surrounding the cysteine residues can also influence disulfide crosslinking efficiency (Singh and Whitesides, 1993).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about factors affecting disulfide formation.

claim: The first step of the thiol-disulfide interchange reaction requires deprotonation of the cysteine sulfhydryl and thus will be facilitated by lowering of the pKa of the cysteine thiol.
source: The first step of the thiol-disulfide interchange reaction requires deprotonation of the cysteine sulfhydryl and thus will be facilitated by lowering of the pKa of the cysteine thiol (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is knowledge about the chemical mechanism of disulfide formation.

claim: Multiple factors could affect the crosslinking efficiency of L1-L1' at the different cysteines on L1, explaining why crosslinking efficiency does not simply correlate with Cα-Cα' distance of the cysteine pairs.
source: Altogether, multiple factors could affect the crosslinking efficiency of L1-L1' at the different cysteines on L1, explaining why crosslinking efficiency does not simply correlate with Cα-Cα' distance of the cysteine pairs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the discussion of factors affecting crosslinking.

claim: Recombinant Xenopus H2A with the corresponding cysteine substitution as yeast Hta1(N39C) and Htz1(T46C) supported efficient L1-L1' crosslinking of histone octamers in vitro.
source: A recent study from the Richmond lab indicated that recombinant Xenopus H2A with the corresponding cysteine substitution as yeast Hta1(N39C) and Htz1(T46C) supported efficient L1-L1' crosslinking of histone octamers in vitro (Frouws et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited work from another lab supporting the crosslinking approach.

claim: The majority of the nucleosomes (including the AA, AZ and ZZ configurations) in the HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C) double mutant are expected to be crosslinked upon 4-DPS treatment.
source: Therefore, the majority of the nucleosomes (including the AA, AZ and ZZ configurations) in the HTA1(N39C) HTZ1(T46C) double mutant in Figure 3 are expected to be crosslinked upon 4-DPS treatment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited in vitro work and the experimental data.

claim: The bulk of the uncrosslinked species should represent the non-nucleosomal pools of A-B and Z-B dimers, which constitute 39% and 26% of total H2A and H2A.Z, respectively.
source: Notwithstanding a minor contribution of the uncrosslinked monomers a result of inefficient crosslinking, the bulk of the uncrosslinked species should represent the non-nucleosomal pools of A-B and Z-B dimers, which constitute 39% and 26% of total H2A and H2A.Z, respectively (Figure 3A lane 6, 3B lane 6, and 3C lanes 2 and 4).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 3.

claim: These unincorporated histones could be A-B and Z-B dimers that are associated with histone chaperones or chromatin remodelers, like SWR.
source: These unincorporated histones could be A-B and Z-B dimers that are associated with histone chaperones or chromatin remodelers, like SWR (Luk et al., 2007; Sun and Luk, 2017; Wu et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with cited support.

claim: These dimers could also be associated with chromatin in the form of hexasomes (partial nucleosomal particles missing one A-B or Z-B dimer) or non-nucleosomal histone-DNA complexes.
source: These dimers could also be associated with chromatin in the form of hexasomes (partial nucleosomal particles missing one A-B or Z-B dimer) or non-nucleosomal histone-DNA complexes (Andrews et al., 2010; Arimura et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with cited support.

claim: Endogenous cysteines that are outside of a ~ 15 Å radius from the intended cysteine probe should not interfere with VivosX and thus need not be removed.
source: However, we argue that endogenous cysteines that are outside of a ~ 15 Å radius from the intended cysteine probe should not interfere with VivosX and thus need not be removed, as the histone mutants Htz1(H44C), Htz1(T49C), and Hta1(G38C) exhibited virtually no crosslinking.
evidence: This is an argument based on the data showing no crosslinking at certain positions.

claim: Endogenous cysteines that are solvent exposed and in proximity to an interaction interface could potentially be exploited as cysteine probes for VivosX.
source: In fact, endogenous cysteines that are solvent exposed and in proximity to an interaction interface could potentially be exploited as cysteine probes for VivosX.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future applications of VivosX.

claim: A cysteine at position 110 (C110) of histone H3, which is conserved in most eukaryotes (but not in yeast), is within disulfide crosslinking distance with the same cysteine on the opposite H3 within nucleosomes.
source: A cysteine at position 110 (C110) of histone H3, which is conserved in most eukaryotes (but not in yeast), is within disulfide crosslinking distance with the same cysteine on the opposite H3 within nucleosomes (Camerini-Otero and Felsenfeld, 1977).
evidence: This is cited knowledge about H3 C110.

claim: No 4-DPS-dependent C110-C110' H3 crosslinking adduct was detected in the non-reducing anti-H3 immunoblot of human H2A.Z VivosX analysis where efficient H2A.Z L1-L1' crosslinking was observed.
source: Interestingly, in the VivosX analysis of human H2A.Z where efficient H2A.Z L1-L1' crosslinking was observed, no 4-DPS-dependent C110-C110' H3 crosslinking adduct was detected in the non-reducing anti-H3 immunoblot (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The lack of H3 C110 crosslinking is consistent with a previous conclusion that the C110 of histone H3 is inaccessible to thiol-specific reagents and requires destabilization of the nucleosome structure to make C110 solvent accessible.
source: This is consistent with a previous conclusion that the C110 of histone H3 is inaccessible to thiol-specific reagents and requires destabilization of the nucleosome structure to make C110 solvent accessible (Johnson et al., 1987).
evidence: This is a comparison with cited literature explaining the lack of H3 crosslinking.

claim: The Cα-Cα' distance for the L1-L1' interface at H43 of human H2A.Z is 8.2 Å, which is 2.6 Å greater than that of the average disulfide bond.
source: The Cα-Cα' distance for the L1-L1' interface at H43 of human H2A.Z is 8.2 Å, which is 2.6 Å greater than that of the average disulfide bond (Schmidt et al., 2006; Suto et al., 2000).
evidence: This is structural information from cited sources.

claim: The ability of H2A.Z(H43C) to efficiently form intra-nucleosomal crosslinks suggests that the L1-L1' interface of ZZ nucleosomes in human cells is not only solvent accessible, but also dynamic as in the case of the yeast ZZ nucleosomes.
source: The ability of H2A.Z(H43C) to efficiently form intra-nucleosomal crosslinks suggests that the L1-L1' interface of ZZ nucleosomes in human cells is not only solvent accessible, but also dynamic as in the case of the yeast ZZ nucleosomes.
evidence: This is an inference from the crosslinking data in human cells.

claim: The observation that monoubiquitylated H2A.Z(H43C) readily forms disulfide crosslinks further supports that the accessibility and dynamics of the H2A.Z L1-L1' interface is independent of transcription.
source: Unlike yeast, however, a subpopulation of H2A.Z in mammalian cells is monoubiquitylated, and these modified H2A.Z molecules are associated with facultative heterochromatin (Sarcinella et al., 2007). The observation that monoubiquitylated H2A.Z(H43C) readily forms disulfide crosslinks further supports that the accessibility and dynamics of the H2A.Z L1-L1' interface is independent of transcription.
evidence: This is an inference from the data showing crosslinking of ubiquitylated H2A.Z in heterochromatin.

claim: VivosX could be used to elucidate the combinatorial interactions of basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) family transcription factors.
source: For example, VivosX could be used to elucidate the combinatorial interactions of basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) family transcription factors.
evidence: This is a suggested future application of VivosX.

claim: Using crystallographic data available for the bHLH-LZ heterodimers, like Myc-Max and Mad-Max, cysteine probes can be placed near the dimerization interface.
source: Using crystallographic data available for the bHLH-LZ heterodimers, like Myc-Max and Mad-Max, cysteine probes can be placed near the dimerization interface (Nair and Burley, 2003).
evidence: This is a suggested approach with cited structural data.

claim: Pairing of different bHLH-LZ dimers and subsequent binding to DNA sites are known to elicit specific cellular responses.
source: As pairing of different bHLH-LZ dimers and subsequent binding to DNA sites are known to elicit specific cellular responses (Diolaiti et al., 2015), the relative abundance of the disulfide adducts between the different bHLH-LZ partners could be used as a metric of pairing status in cells and analyzed by VivosX in a spatiotemporal manner.

claim: VivosX can be used to determine the stoichiometry of post-translational modifications (especially ubiquitin or SUMO) on other non-histone dimers or oligomers.
source: The observation that ZZ nucleosomes can be monoubiquitylated asymmetrically on one H2A.Z or symmetrically on both raises the possibility that VivosX can be used to determine the stoichiometry of post-translational modifications (especially ubiquitin or SUMO) on other non-histone dimers or oligomers.
